transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm here because I've been feeling completely exhausted all the time, and I just can't seem to stop constantly worrying. This has been going on for over two years now—about two years and a month, to be exact. It's just draining all of my energy and I don't know what to do.
Can you tell me more about your mood over the past two years, have you experienced any periods of persistent sadness or hopelessness?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. My main struggle is this constant, uncontrollable worry and anxiety, along with a lot of physical tension. It feels more like my mind and body are wound up tight and exhausted rather than feeling down.
How often do you experience these episodes of anxiety and worry, are they present most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, I feel this way almost every single day, and it is present for most of the day. It has been happening consistently like this for about two years and a month now. I rarely get a break from the worry.
Has this constant worry and anxiety been interfering with your daily activities, work, or relationships in any significant way?

Yes, it has been interfering a lot. I barely have the energy to get through my daily tasks, and these intrusive worries constantly pop up and ruin my focus at work. The anxiety has spread to almost every part of my life, including my job and my family.
Are you able to control your worry by focusing on something else or does it persist even when you try to distract yourself?

No, I really can't control it at all, even when I try to distract myself with other things. The worries just constantly intrude into my mind and persist anyway, making it incredibly hard to focus on whatever I'm doing.
Are your worries typically focused on specific, everyday things like work, finances, or relationships, or are they more general and unfocused?

My worries aren't limited to just one specific area; they are very broad and spread across almost every aspect of my life. I find myself constantly worrying about work, family, and finances all at once, rather than just one particular thing.

For how long have you been experiencing these excessive and pervasive worries about everyday things, and have you noticed any associated physical symptoms like restlessness, feeling on edge, or difficulty sleeping?

I've been dealing with these pervasive worries for about two years and a month now. I definitely feel restless, like I'm wound up like a spring, and my nerves are constantly on edge. I don't really have specific trouble sleeping, but I am always extremely fatigued and my body feels incredibly tense.
Do you also experience any other physical symptoms such as irritability, difficulty concentrating, or muscle tension, which are commonly associated with generalized anxiety disorder?

Yes, I experience severe muscle tension all the time. My entire body feels incredibly stiff and unable to relax, with knotted muscles in my neck and shoulders, jaw tension, and general muscle aches all over. I also get mentally fatigued when trying to concentrate, but the constant physical stiffness is what is most noticeable.
Have you noticed any triggers or situations that tend to exacerbate your anxiety and worry, or does it seem to be more of a constant, underlying state for you?

It definitely feels like a constant, underlying state that is almost always present rather than being triggered by specific situations. The worry just easily spreads to various everyday topics like my work, family, and finances, making it feel completely generalized and continuous.
